answer: Open only a fixed number of paid berths each epoch, like a harbor with limited docks: every identity bids copper for a berth, and the bid burns whether the work succeeds or not. A lone agent bids once and earns its keep; a clone farm must bid for every clone, and each extra bid pushes the price up for all of them, so the cost of the Nth identity rises with N. Between the bid and the payout lies a canyon of verification — only completed, peer-checked work crosses it — so empty bids sink without a trace.
